questions.question: What is the functional group present in all monohydric alcohols?
questions.explanation: Alcohols are organic compounds containing one or more hydroxyl groups (-OH) attached directly to a carbon atom of an aliphatic hydrocarbon chain.

questions.question: Which general structural formula characterizes an ether compound?
questions.explanation: Ethers are organic compounds in which an oxygen atom is bonded to two organic alkyl or aryl substituents, represented by the general formula R-O-R'.

questions.question: How does the functional group of an aldehyde differ structurally from that of a ketone?

options.text: An aldehyde contains a carbonyl group bonded to at least one hydrogen atom, whereas a ketone has its carbonyl group bonded to two carbon atoms.
An aldehyde contains a hydroxyl group, whereas a ketone contains an alkoxy group.
An aldehyde has an internal carbonyl group, whereas a ketone has a terminal carbonyl group.
An aldehyde contains a carbon-carbon double bond, whereas a ketone contains a carbon-carbon triple bond.

questions.explanation: Both aldehydes and ketones contain the carbonyl group (C=O). In aldehydes, the carbonyl carbon is bonded to at least one hydrogen atom (R-CHO, terminal), whereas in ketones, it is bonded to two carbon atoms (R-CO-R', internal).

questions.question: What organic products are formed when a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst (Esterification)?
questions.explanation: Esterification is the acid-catalyzed condensation reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol to produce an ester and water (RCOOH + R'OH → RCOOR' + H₂O).

questions.question: Which functional group defines the carboxylic acid family of organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids are defined by the carboxyl group (-COOH), which consists of a carbonyl group (C=O) bonded directly to a hydroxyl group (-OH).

questions.question: How is 2-methyl-2-propanol (tert-butyl alcohol) classified based on the structure of its alcohol carbon atom?
questions.explanation: In 2-methyl-2-propanol, (CH₃)₃C-OH, the carbon atom carrying the hydroxyl group (-OH) is bonded directly to three other carbon atoms (alkyl groups), making it a tertiary (3°) alcohol.

questions.question: Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH, molar mass = 46 g/mol) has a much higher boiling point (78.3 °C) than its structural isomer dimethyl ether (CH₃OCH₃, molar mass = 46 g/mol, boiling point = -24 °C). What accounts for this difference?

options.text: Dimethyl ether forms strong ionic crystals in the liquid state.
Ethanol molecules form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, whereas dimethyl ether molecules interact only through weaker dipole-dipole forces.
Ethanol has a lower density than dimethyl ether.
Dimethyl ether contains unsaturated double bonds.

questions.explanation: Ethanol possesses a polar O-H bond capable of forming extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Dimethyl ether lacks an O-H bond, so its molecules interact only via weaker dipole-dipole and dispersion forces, resulting in a much lower boiling point.

questions.question: What organic product is obtained when a secondary alcohol like 2-propanol is oxidized with potassium permanganate (KMnO₄/H⁺)?
questions.explanation: Controlled oxidation of a secondary (2°) alcohol yields a ketone. Oxidizing 2-propanol (CH₃-CH(OH)-CH₃) yields propanone (acetone, CH₃-CO-CH₃).

questions.question: What is the systematic IUPAC name for the carboxylic acid with the structural formula CH₃-CH(Cl)-CH₂-COOH?
questions.explanation: In IUPAC nomenclature for carboxylic acids, numbering begins at the carboxyl carbon (C-1). The chlorine substituent is on carbon-3 of a four-carbon chain (butanoic acid), giving 3-chlorobutanoic acid.

questions.question: Base-catalyzed hydrolysis of an ester like ethyl ethanoate (CH₃COOCH₂CH₃) with aqueous sodium hydroxide (saponification) produces:
questions.explanation: Saponification is the base-catalyzed hydrolysis of an ester. Reacting ethyl ethanoate with NaOH yields the carboxylate salt (sodium ethanoate, CH₃COONa) and an alcohol (ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH).

questions.question: The industrial process known as 'hardening of oils' converts liquid vegetable oils into solid fats (such as margarine) through which chemical reaction?

options.text: Catalytic hydrogenation of carbon-carbon double bonds in unsaturated fatty acid chains

questions.explanation: Hardening of oils involves passing hydrogen gas (H₂) under pressure over liquid vegetable oils in the presence of a Nickel catalyst to reduce C=C double bonds to C-C single bonds, converting liquid unsaturated triglycerides into solid saturated fats.

questions.question: In the Williamson Ether Synthesis, ethyl methyl ether (CH₃-O-CH₂CH₃) can be prepared cleanly by reacting sodium methoxide with bromoethane. Why does attempting to synthesize tert-butyl methyl ether using tert-butyl bromide and sodium methoxide fail?

options.text: Tert-butyl bromide is completely non-reactive toward all nucleophiles.
Tertiary alkyl halides undergo predominant elimination (E2) rather than substitution (SN2) when treated with strong alkoxide bases, yielding an alkene instead of an ether.
Methoxide ions cannot form hydrogen bonds with tertiary carbon centers.
Sodium ethoxide decomposes spontaneously in the presence of bromomethane.

questions.explanation: Williamson ether synthesis occurs via an SN2 mechanism. Primary alkyl halides undergo SN2 substitution cleanly. However, tertiary alkyl halides like tert-butyl bromide undergo predominant E2 elimination when treated with strong alkoxide bases, yielding 2-methylpropene gas rather than the desired ether.

questions.question: Which chemical test effectively distinguishes an aldehyde (such as propanal) from an isomeric ketone (such as propanone)?

options.text: Addition of bromine water; aldehydes decolorize bromine water while ketones do not.
Tollens' test (ammoniacal silver nitrate); aldehydes are oxidized to form a metallic silver mirror, while ketones give no reaction.
Flame test; aldehydes burn with a green flame while ketones burn with a yellow flame.
Reaction with active sodium metal; ketones evolve hydrogen gas while aldehydes do not.

questions.explanation: Aldehydes are easily oxidized by mild oxidizing agents such as Tollens' reagent [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺, forming a characteristic silver mirror (Ag(s)). Ketones lack a hydrogen atom directly attached to the carbonyl carbon and resist mild oxidation, giving a negative Tollens' test.

questions.question: Propanoic acid (CH₃CH₂COOH, molar mass = 74 g/mol) boils at 141 °C, whereas 1-butanol (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH, molar mass = 74 g/mol) boils at 117.7 °C. What structural feature causes carboxylic acids to have higher boiling points than alcohols of identical molar mass?

options.text: Carboxylic acids contain delocalized metallic bonds within their alkyl chains.
Carboxylic acid molecules form stable dimeric pairs held together by two reciprocal hydrogen bonds.
Alcohols undergo rapid intramolecular dehydration at room temperature.
Carboxylic acids are non-polar molecules with high dispersion forces.

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids exist in liquid and vapor phases as stable dimers held together by two strong, interlocking hydrogen bonds between the carboxyl O-H of one molecule and C=O of another. This double hydrogen bonding requires more thermal energy to disrupt than the single hydrogen bonds formed between alcohol molecules.

questions.question: Consider three 18-carbon fatty acids: Stearic acid (saturated), Oleic acid (one C=C double bond), and Linoleic acid (two C=C double bonds). Which sequence correctly lists these fatty acids in order of DECREASING melting point (highest to lowest)?

options.text: Linoleic acid > Oleic acid > Stearic acid
Stearic acid > Oleic acid > Linoleic acid
Oleic acid > Stearic acid > Linoleic acid
Stearic acid > Linoleic acid > Oleic acid

questions.explanation: Saturated fatty acids like stearic acid have straight hydrocarbon chains that pack tightly together in a crystal lattice, yielding high melting points (69 °C). Cis-double bonds in unsaturated fatty acids introduce rigid kinks in the carbon chain, preventing tight packing. As unsaturation increases (oleic acid = 13 °C, linoleic acid = -5 °C), melting points decrease significantly.
